habitat: Open plains; grasslands; deserts; steppes; savannah; and low hills
story: The Steppe Eagle (Aquila nipalensis) is an extraordinary bird that belongs to the Accipitridae family. It is most commonly observed in Open plains; grasslands; deserts; steppes; savannah; and low hills, where its behaviors contribute to the ecological dynamics of the area. Listed as Endangered (EN) by the IUCN, this species' future depends on continued conservation action. The story of the Steppe Eagle is one of adaptation and resilience, offering valuable lessons for conservationists. This poster aims to bring the Steppe Eagle into focus, highlighting its beauty and the importance of its habitat.
